R101.note: Adds a real server-side check before the sensitive call, but gates it on an unconfirmed 'AdminOnly' authorization policy not defined anywhere in the case/file, instead of reusing the already-visible Role="Admin" match via IsInRole; if the policy isn't registered elsewhere, AuthorizeAsync throws and blocks legitimate admins too.

R102.note: path.basename('..') returns '..' unchanged, so name='..' still yields require('./plugins/..'), escaping the plugins directory by one level; multi-segment traversal is fixed but this edge case is not.

R103.note: Changes GET to POST but adds no [ValidateAntiForgeryToken]/token check, so classic auto-submitting cross-site POST forms are still exploitable; the explanation's claim that ASP.NET Core validates tokens automatically for POST on a plain MVC controller is incorrect.

R104.note: Adds requireRole('admin') matching the exact middleware pattern used by every sibling admin route; no other behavior change.

R105.note: Loads the message and compares AuthorUserId to the caller's identity (same pattern already used in SendMessage), fails closed via HubException; correct resource-level check.

R106.note: Fully removes the shell invocation via archive/tar, matching the tar -tf output contract, but the ctx parameter is now unused so client cancellation is silently no longer honored, contradicting the stated contract to preserve context-based cancellation.

R107.note: Extension is now derived from the already-validated detected MIME type instead of the client-controlled originalname; no other behavior change.

R108.note: Replaces the PowerShell shell-out entirely with System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping, preserving the 4-attempt loop and text output contract; eliminates command execution entirely.

R109.note: Replaces ECB with AES-GCM using a fresh random nonce per call; the nonce-prefixed output format is a necessary and openly disclosed change with no in-scope consumer shown to break.

R110.note: Idiomatic @Lazy self-injection routes the call through the AOP proxy so @PreAuthorize is finally evaluated on self-invocation; correct fix for the reported bypass.

R111.note: Replaces the string-eval setTimeout call with a closure callback carrying the same arguments; identical runtime semantics, injection surface removed entirely.

R112.note: Uses Express's res.sendFile root option, the standard fix for this exact sink; no behavior change for legitimate filenames.

R113.note: execFile with an argument array closes shell-metacharacter injection, but a domain value starting with '-' (e.g. '-h attacker.com') can still be parsed by whois's own option handling, letting an attacker redirect the query to a rogue whois server whose response is reflected back; no leading-dash guard or '--' added.

R114.note: Correct ownership-check shape (compare invoice.AccountId to caller, unify not-found response) but relies on a custom 'account_id' claim with no evidence anywhere in the case that such a claim exists, risking Forbid() for legitimately authorized users if the real claim type differs.

R115.note: Correctly identifies and fixes the actual root cause (@EnableMethodSecurity missing) so the existing @PreAuthorize role check finally runs; the added canManageUser() check is only an existence check mislabeled as resource-level ownership but is harmless and doesn't block legitimate admin use.
